questions.q: Which five disciplines does Senge say turn a workplace into a learning organization?
a: Personal mastery, mental models, team learning, shared vision, systems thinking
Clear goals, tight budgets, strong managers, fast feedback, fair pay
Hiring, training, promotion, retention, succession planning
Strategy, structure, systems, staff, and shared values
questions.why: Lesson 2 names those five disciplines, ending with systems thinking as the integrating one.

questions.q: Which discipline does lesson 2 call the most important and the one that integrates the rest?
a: Systems thinking
Personal mastery
Team learning
Shared vision
questions.why: Lesson 2 says systems thinking looks at problems as a whole and ties all five together.

questions.q: What does shared vision mean in a learning organization?
a: Employees feel ownership of the company's direction
A charismatic leader hands down a fixed plan
Every team writes its own separate mission
Vision statements are posted in every office
questions.why: Lesson 2 contrasts shared vision with a visionary leader simply imposing their ideas.

questions.q: What three roles should leaders adopt instead of focusing on titles?
a: Designer, teacher, and steward
Coach, referee, and scorekeeper
Planner, controller, and inspector
Founder, manager, and investor
questions.why: Lesson 3 says leaders must become designers, teachers, and stewards.

questions.q: What does the story of the slowly heated frog illustrate about companies?
a: They fail to notice problems that grow gradually
They adapt best when change happens slowly
They need warmer, more comfortable offices
They should avoid making any long-term plans
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the frog to show reactive firms miss slowly worsening problems.
